title: How a Lawn Mower Works in 60 Seconds 🌱⚙️ #shorts
description:
A rotary mower spins one steel blade at roughly 3,000 RPM, and safety rules cap the blade tip at 19,000 feet per minute, over 200 mph. The blade's tips are bent up into wings that suck grass upright and throw clippings into the bag. Raising the wheels sets how tall the lawn stays. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#lawnmower #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A mower blade tip can move at over *200 miles per hour*.

steps.label: Engine
steps.text: A small *engine* or motor turns a vertical shaft about *3,000 times* a minute.

steps.label: Blade
steps.text: One steel *blade* bolts to that shaft, spinning flat just above the *grass*.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: It doesn't slice like scissors. The fast edge *whacks* each blade of grass *clean off*.

steps.label: Lift
steps.text: Bent-up *wings* on the blade suck air up, standing the grass tall and *blowing clippings* into the bag.

steps.label: Height
steps.text: Raise or lower the *wheels*, and you set how *tall* your lawn stays.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, whack, *bag*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
